title: Dominic and the Spire
premise: Lena Hartwell's double life as royal food-taster and ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things collapses when a century-old prophecy book names tonight's date as the night the Spire claims its due. The soul in question belongs to Dominic, the guild's smuggler-archivist who once sold his own soul to buy Lena's freedom, and the court beneath the mountain has come to collect. To save him, Lena must assemble a found family of debtors, forgers, and exiles, break into the Spire itself, and discover that the prophecy was written by her own future self — meaning she can rewrite it only by paying a price of equal weight. In the end she trades her memories of Dominic to void the contract, and he chooses to win them back one impossible thing at a time.
about_author: Lior Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent seven years cataloguing other people's unfinished letters before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep records of things that were never supposed to happen.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She tastes the king's supper, catalogues three poisons by aftertaste, and slips home to the guildhall where she balances ledgers of traded impossibilities. Establishes her precision and loneliness; ends with Dominic teasing her about never writing herself into any record.

chapters.title: A Date in Old Ink
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. While shelving the prophecy folios she finds tomorrow's exact date circled in century-old ink beside a name: Hartwell. She assumes forgery until the handwriting matches her own. Fear arrives not as panic but as an accounting error she cannot balance.

chapters.title: The Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He introduces the guild's strange economy — bottled last words, borrowed luck, one honest lie — and reveals he knows what the prophecy says. He lies smoothly about it being nothing, but the reader sees him hide a contract bearing his own signature.

chapters.title: What Dominic Sold
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Digging through the vault ledgers she finds it: ten years ago Dominic sold his soul to the court beneath the mountain to purchase a pardon for a girl condemned as a taster's scapegoat. Her. The chapter ends on the collection clause: due when the prophecy's date arrives.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Ledger Desk
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lena confronts Dominic; he refuses apology, insisting the trade was fair and final. Their argument cracks the guild's easy intimacy. Beat: love expressed as stubbornness, both too proud to say the true thing.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Wren, a debtor-spy POV. Below the city, the subterranean court sharpens its claim on Dominic's soul; its magistrate reads the prophecy aloud like a menu. Introduces antagonist logic: the court does not want cruelty, it wants precedent — contracts must hold or everything unravels.

chapters.title: The First Impossible Thing
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She asks the guild how to void a soul-contract; the answer is always the same: pay something of equal weight. She begins listing candidates — her taster's immunity, her guild membership, her memories. Ends with her circling 'memories' and hating her own handwriting.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Forger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She seeks Odile Vasse, a disgraced court calligrapher who can forge anything except forgiveness. Odile agrees to help falsify the contract's provenance — if Lena steals back Odile's confiscated name from the Spire's registry. A bargain is struck.

chapters.title: The Debtors' Table
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Wren POV. Wren defects from the court, bringing maps of the under-mountain and a warning: the magistrate suspects interference. At the debtors' table, outcasts argue strategy; Dominic arrives uninvited and refuses to be rescued. Fracture lines form in the plan.

chapters.title: Prophecy Mechanics
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Studying the prophecy book, she finds marginalia in Lena's hand dated decades ahead — notes correcting earlier entries. The horrifying implication lands: the book is written backward, and future-Lena authored it. Free will becomes a question of margins.

chapters.title: The King's Poisoner
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Back at court, a new poison appears that no antidote covers — unless it isn't poison but pressure: someone wants the taster dead before the date. She survives by wit and a forged allergy, realizing the court has agents above ground. Stakes tighten.

chapters.title: Ten Years Ago
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV flashback. The full story of the sale: young Dominic, the scapegoat trial, the descent to the court, the magistrate's velvet terms. He signed knowing exactly what memory costs because he'd already watched his mother forget him. Reframes his secrecy as protection.

chapters.title: The Registry of Names
chapters.summary: Planning chapter, ensemble. Wren diagrams the Spire: a tower grown downward into the mountain, its heart a registry where every sold name is written. To free Dominic they must strike his entry; to free Odile's name, steal the page whole. Two thefts, one night.

chapters.title: Practice Run
chapters.summary: Lena and Odile POV interleave. They rehearse the infiltration in the guildhall using chalk outlines and borrowed luck from stock. It fails hilariously, then almost works. Between failures, Odile asks why Lena would spend her memories; Lena realizes she doesn't have an answer that isn't love.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Offer
chapters.summary: Wren POV. The magistrate summons Wren back and offers reinstatement plus Dominic's contract torn up — if Wren delivers Lena instead. Wren stalls, buys three days, and returns to the surface carrying the offer like a stone. Loyalty tested with a clean, reasonable price.

chapters.title: Confession Over Cold Tea
chapters.summary: Two-hander, Lena and Dominic. Wren confesses the offer; Dominic says take it. Lena, furious, finally names what the sale meant: he bought her life without asking, just as she plans to buy his. They agree, at last, to make the choice together — whatever it costs either.

chapters.title: Descent Day
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The prophecy's date dawns. The team descends through the salt mines: Odile with forged credentials, Wren leading, Dominic under guard disguised as cargo (his idea). Above, the king's poisoner watches them go. Chapter ends at the door that only opens for the owed.

chapters.title: The Velvet Corridors
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Inside, the court is terrible in a bureaucratic way — endless waiting rooms, polite ushers, forms in triplicate. Odile's forgery passes inspection twice, then wobbles. Wren burns a favor to get them through. Humor braided with mounting tension.

chapters.title: The Waiting Room of the Owed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They find others waiting to be collected: souls sold cheaply generations ago, patient as furniture. An old woman recognizes Dominic's name and blesses their theft. Lena understands the scale of the court's holdings — and that freeing one soul indicts the system.

chapters.title: Separation
chapters.summary: Ensemble, quick cuts. An audit sweeps the corridors; the group scatters. Wren draws the pursuers, Odile reaches the registry annex alone, and Lena is escorted — politely, irrevocably — to the magistrate's chamber. Each believes they are the diversion now.

chapters.title: Audience with the Magistrate
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The magistrate is courteous, even kind, and offers Lena the original deal inverted: her memories for Dominic's soul, exactly as she planned — the court will simply formalize it. The horror: her sacrifice is already priced, expected, prophesied. She asks for time to sign.

chapters.title: The Registry Heart
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Alone in the annex, Odile finds her own confiscated name and cannot lift the page without triggering alarms. She chooses to copy rather than steal — a forgery of herself — and discovers Dominic's entry bears an annotation in Lena's future-handwriting: 'voided, see p. 412.'

chapters.title: Page 412
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, mid-negotiation. She stalls the magistrate by requesting the master ledger, page 412. It exists: a blank page except for one line in her handwriting — 'paid in full, remember to forget.' The prophecy loop closes visibly. She signs nothing yet.

chapters.title: Wren's Stand
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Cornered in the salt galleries, Wren fights not to escape but to buy minutes, using every court procedure against the court. Captured, they tell the magistrate the truth: the offer was refused hours ago. Dignity in defeat; the alarm sounds anyway.

chapters.title: The Equal Weight Problem
chapters.summary: Lena and Dominic, reunited briefly under guard. Dominic learns the price and forbids it; Lena shows him page 412 — it's already done, somewhere, sometime. If the note is true, her memories are already gone in some version of events. Despair and strange comfort share a line.

chapters.title: Odile's Name, Returned
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The forged page passes final inspection; Odile walks out owning her own name again — legally a person the court never held. On the way she frees the old woman from the waiting room with a clerk's stamp and a straight face. Small justices compound.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Climax begins, Lena's POV. At the registry heart, before witnesses, Lena initiates the trade: her memories of Dominic, itemized and weighed. The court's scales accept. As the first memories lift — the guildhall, the tea, his laugh — she keeps talking, narrating them to the room so the words remain even when the feeling goes.

chapters.title: Voided, See Page 412
chapters.summary: Climax turns, Dominic's POV. Freed as the contract dissolves, Dominic does the impossible thing no one priced: he writes a new entry in the prophecy book's margin — 'returned, with interest' — and demands the court honor its own precedents. The magistrate, bound by law above malice, must comply. The soul comes home.

chapters.title: Ascension
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The five climb out of the mountain at dawn, minus one set of memories. Dominic carries Lena, who looks at him with perfect politeness and no recognition. The old woman's blessing follows them up like light. Victory and loss in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Ledger Desk
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Weeks later: she tastes, she files, she sleeps well. Dominic works beside her as a courteous colleague. She keeps finding her own marginalia she doesn't remember writing, all pointing toward a man she can't place. Grief without an object.

chapters.title: Records of a Life
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He refuses to let the forgetting stand. Following her own advice — narrated memories witnessed by the court — he reconstructs their history in a private ledger: every tea, every argument, page 412's promise. He decides to repay the debt the only way the guild knows: impossible things, one at a time.

chapters.title: Borrowed Luck
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Odd gifts begin appearing in her quarters: a bottle of last words, a coin that lands kindly, a letter in her own hand describing a man worth remembering. She investigates as a taster would — testing, doubting — and starts to feel haunted in a warm way.

chapters.title: The Court's Audit
chapters.summary: Wren POV. The subterranean court, stung by precedent, audits itself; souls sold cheaply are being reweighed. The magistrate sends word: the exchange was legal, but the interest clause — 'with interest' — remains open-ended. What Dominic claimed back may be reclaimable in kind.

chapters.title: Interest Due
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following the ledger trail, Lena descends voluntarily to the court and invokes the interest clause herself: if her memories were payment, their return is owed. The magistrate, respecting a well-argued claim more than any plea, grants a hearing. She stands where Dominic once stood.

chapters.title: The Hearing of Hartwell
chapters.summary: Courtroom chapter, multiple POVs. Dominic testifies with the reconstructed ledger; Odile authenticates every hand; Wren cites precedent; the old woman speaks for the waiting room. Against a century of contracts, the guild argues that memory freely given and freely reclaimed sets new law.

chapters.title: Remember to Forget
chapters.summary: Climax of the return, Lena's POV. The court rules: the memories return, but she must choose which single memory stays paid forever — the scales demand balance. She keeps the forgetting of one small afternoon, a price she pays smiling, because a self should keep one mystery.

chapters.title: Tea, Again
chapters.summary: Two-hander. Memories flood back mid-conversation; Lena finishes a sentence Dominic started ten years ago. No dramatic reunion — just two people picking up an argument about whether the trade was fair, and this time answering honestly. Quiet, complete joy.

chapters.title: Amendments
chapters.summary: Ensemble resolution. The guild rewrites its charter: no soul-sales, memory-trades regulated, the waiting room emptied by decree and by paperwork. Odile teaches calligraphy; Wren runs the court's reform office from inside; the old woman tends a garden above ground for the first time in sixty years.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Lena's POV coda. She writes the prophecy book's final margin note in her own present-tense hand: 'the date passed; we chose.' On the desk, one blank page labeled 413 waits for whatever impossible thing comes next. She closes the ledger, pours two cups of tea, and calls Dominic in from the rain.
